items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: but I'm going to take you, you got a job. He said I got a son just about your age

ctx.x: tickled to death. Finally--which I learned later from experience--they were all happy over me, but this trumpet player that was sitting next to, I think--I know, because he saw I was reading it to a tee but (inaudible), and he said let's jam a little, and Eddie said, you're the very one who didn't want to rehearse, and here's this man that came here and played the hardest stuff we have in the book, what do you want to bother him for, let him go back to his job, the man has a job. You didn't want to rehearse…

does too, but he stutters very bad and he goes ba-ba-ba-ba-I never seen nobody play that much music and play a damn thing; but I'm going to take you, you got a job. He said I got a son just about your age, you got the foundation, I'm going to make a musician out of you. He said how in the world did you read all that music and can't play nothing. So I said I haven't been doing anything like that. Well, that's all right, I'm going to carry you with me.
Do you remember the number that they were jamming?
